items.question: On what ontological ground must the modifications in question be denied existence rather than denied mere distinction from their source?
premises: The modifications are not distinct from those modes specified in the preceding verses.
Modifications are only posited in relation to a root as their source.
If no distinct modifications of the root are admitted, no such modifications can exist.
items.inference: Since the modifications are not distinct from the previously named modes and cannot stand as distinct from the root, they do not exist.
uncertainties: The precise anaphoric reach of ābhyaḥ depends strictly on v223–v224 and is not recoverable from this verse alone.
items.plain_english: The modifications are not distinct from these; therefore, as modifications distinct from the root, they do not exist.
